_comment: Catalogue v0.1 — seed set from MASTER_BUILD_SWAP_TEST.md Phase 3.2; v0.1.1 sharpened F01-F04/F06 triggers after eval round 1 over-flagged reflective working-style sentences in gold letters (6.78→1.84 false failures/letter); v0.1.2 adds intrinsic criteria — failures mark FAKE evidence, positioning sentences are neither technique nor failure, validated against the corpus's own worked example (Appendix A). Trigger phrasing is what eval iteration tunes (Phase 5). PENDING HUMAN GATE review before public launch. Exemplars are anonymised: Appendix A verified letters + bracket-anonymised gold snippets only (anonymisation CI: tests/swap-anonymisation.test.ts).

techniques.name: Quantified self-initiative
techniques.definition: Something the applicant started or built unprompted, with a magnitude attached.
techniques.trigger: A self-started action plus a number (users, revenue, savings, rating). Both must be present, and the action must be the applicant's own initiative rather than an assigned task.
techniques.exemplar: A tool I built over three weekends now has 4,200 active users

techniques.name: Before/after with baseline
techniques.definition: A metric stated with its starting value and its ending value.
techniques.trigger: A baseline AND an end state for the same metric — 'from A to B' shapes, or an explicit delta over a stated period. A lone end state without its baseline does not qualify.
techniques.exemplar: 11 experiments over two quarters lifted trial starts from 6.1% to 8.4%.

techniques.name: Named failure before the win
techniques.definition: A failed attempt named explicitly before the eventual success.
techniques.trigger: Words like 'failed', 'didn't work', 'missed', or 'wrong' describing the applicant's own attempt, appearing before or alongside the win it led to.
techniques.exemplar: The first three tests failed outright — the real win came from re-ordering the paywall, not redesigning it.

techniques.name: Constraint showing judgment
techniques.definition: A limitation stated together with the decision it forced.
techniques.trigger: A named constraint (budget, time, headcount, tooling) plus the trade-off or decision the applicant made because of it. The constraint alone is not enough.
techniques.exemplar: With no budget for paid acquisition, I cut the onboarding flow to two screens instead

techniques.name: Employer decision referenced
techniques.definition: A specific decision, launch, or change the employer actually made.
techniques.trigger: A concrete, dateable move by this employer — a launch, bundle, pricing change, acquisition, expansion — named specifically. Their mission, values, or category standing do NOT qualify.
techniques.exemplar: Chorusline's move to bundle Daily Mix with the family plan is exactly the conversion problem I've spent two years on.

techniques.name: Employer problem diagnosed
techniques.definition: A problem the employer plausibly has, framed from evidence.
techniques.trigger: The applicant names a specific problem or gap on the employer's side, grounded in something observable (their funnel, pricing page, posting, public metrics) — analysis, not praise.
techniques.exemplar: your checkout still asks for a card before the trial starts, which is where I'd expect the drop-off

techniques.name: Product used as customer
techniques.definition: First-hand use of the employer's product with an observation only a user would have.
techniques.trigger: Evidence of actually using the product (a feature detail, a workflow quirk, a moment of friction) that could not be written from the marketing site alone.
techniques.exemplar: after two months on the free tier I noticed the export button disappears on mobile

techniques.name: Posting detail engaged
techniques.definition: A specific line of the posting engaged with new information.
techniques.trigger: A requirement or detail from the job ad taken up and ADVANCED — challenged, extended, or connected to the applicant's evidence. Restating it does not qualify (that is F05).
techniques.exemplar: exactly the conversion problem I've spent two years on

techniques.name: Concrete first step
techniques.definition: A specific action the applicant would take in the role.
techniques.trigger: A named first action — what they would audit, build, measure, or ship first — specific enough to disagree with. Generic eagerness to 'contribute' does not qualify.
techniques.exemplar: The first thing I'd audit is the order of the paywall screens against your trial data

techniques.name: Scope stated precisely
techniques.definition: The exact ownership boundary of the applicant's work.
techniques.trigger: What the applicant owned, on which surface, for how long — precise enough that an interviewer could probe the edges of it.
techniques.exemplar: At my current app, I owned free-to-paid activation

techniques.name: Method named
techniques.definition: The named technique or process behind a result.
techniques.trigger: A concrete method (experiment design, framework, tooling, process) named as the mechanism of a result — not adjectives about approach ('analytical', 'rigorous').

techniques.name: Public statement referenced
techniques.definition: A public statement by the employer referenced specifically.
techniques.trigger: A quote, blog post, interview, talk, or announcement from the employer referenced with enough specificity to identify the actual source.
techniques.exemplar: your CTO's post on why you rebuilt the recommendation stack in-house

failures.name: Verb without magnitude
failures.definition: An achievement verb with no number, baseline, or named result.
failures.trigger: Verbs like 'improved', 'increased', 'strengthened', 'drove', 'optimised' carrying no magnitude and no named artefact — the reader cannot size the claim. Only when the unquantified achievement IS the sentence's core claim — observations, lessons, or patterns drawn from work ('the pattern across all three was the same') are not achievement claims. Requires BOTH no number AND no named artefact or outcome — a sentence naming what was built and who used it ('models managing directors took into client meetings') has substance and is never F01. An achievement claim leaning on a vague intensifier ('significantly', 'substantially', 'greatly', 'dramatically') with no number is ALWAYS F01.
failures.exemplar: In my current role I improved onboarding, strengthened retention, and partnered closely with design and engineering.

failures.name: Self-rating
failures.definition: A self-assigned trait with no evidence attached.
failures.trigger: Traits the applicant grants themselves — 'data-driven', 'passionate', 'strategic thinker', 'natural leader' — without the result or method that would earn them. F02 is a BARE adjective list ('I am hardworking, motivated, and a fast learner'). A description of concrete working practices ('I write PRDs, run discovery, test assumptions with data') or a specific reputation ('known for catching the error in the appendix') is never F02.
failures.exemplar: I'm a data-driven leader with a genuine passion for music and technology.

failures.name: Category praise
failures.definition: Praise that fits every company in the category.
failures.trigger: Compliments that would survive unchanged at any competitor — mission admiration, 'commitment to innovation', 'industry leader'. If swapping the company name breaks nothing, it is F03. Flag only praise doing the work of research. A sentence about the applicant's own preferences or fit that happens to reference the team or company is not F03. Only sentences whose function is COMPLIMENTING the company. Statements of the applicant's own criteria or wants ('I am looking for a team where…', 'I want to work somewhere that…') are never F03.
failures.exemplar: Chorusline's commitment to putting artists first is something I deeply believe in.

failures.name: Tenure as achievement
failures.definition: Years of experience presented as the achievement itself.
failures.trigger: Duration offered as the substance of the claim — 'with over six years of experience' — with no scope or outcome attached to the years. Flag only when the years are offered as the proof itself. Years mentioned while describing what the work taught, built, or changed are not F04. If the same sentence also carries a number or a named outcome, it is NEVER F04 — years alongside results is context, not the claim.
failures.exemplar: As a product manager with over six years of experience in consumer subscription apps, I've led cross-functional teams through discovery, experimentation, and launch.

failures.name: Requirement restated
failures.definition: A posting requirement repeated back as a qualification.
failures.trigger: The ad's own language mirrored back — 'you need X; I have X' — adding nothing the posting didn't already say. Only when mirroring the posting's requirement language back ('you need X; I have X'). Statements of interest in the employer's work or market are never F05.
failures.exemplar: I have extensive experience with cross-functional stakeholder management, as your posting requires

failures.name: Close without next step
failures.definition: A closing that requests nothing and proposes nothing.
failures.trigger: Sign-off sentences that end the letter without a concrete action — 'I look forward to hearing from you', 'thank you for your consideration' — when nothing before them proposed a step either. Never flag a close that proposes any step, however soft ('I would welcome a technical conversation'). Only the empty formula, with no proposal anywhere in the letter, counts.
failures.exemplar: I look forward to hearing from you and hope to discuss this opportunity further

failures.name: Excitement opener
failures.definition: An opening whose only content is enthusiasm.
failures.trigger: First live sentence built on 'excited to apply', 'thrilled to see', or equivalent — enthusiasm about the role with no information about employer or applicant.
failures.exemplar: I'm excited to apply for the Senior Product Manager role at Chorusline.

failures.name: Unbroken success narrative
failures.definition: Wins stacked with no failure, obstacle, or trade-off anywhere.
failures.trigger: A sentence stacking multiple unqualified wins as part of an all-wins narrative — no attempt named that didn't work, no constraint, no cost. Requires multiple distinct WIN claims stacked in one breath. A single value statement about how the applicant works is not F08 — but two or more unqualified WIN claims joined in one sentence always are.
failures.exemplar: I consistently exceeded every target, delivered every launch on time, and earned top ratings across all my roles
